cultural.vision_reason: This is a 19th-century engraved illustration ("THE CONSULTATION" from Lucas's 1861 work on the Cape/South African peoples) depicting Xhosa men wrapped in kaross-style blankets, carrying spears, with beadwork/necklace ornament and a headdress feather, plus a scene of figures under a tree in the background — consistent with documentary depictions of Xhosa dress and life.

This 19th-century engraving depicts Gaika men (Rharhabe Xhosa, Sandile's people) seated before a beehive hut, wearing traditional beaded ornaments and kaross/blanket wraps, with figures carrying vessels and fowl nearby — a documentary illustration of Xhosa daily life and dress.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a colonial-era engraving depicting a "skirmish" between mounted British/colonial soldiers and Xhosa warriors near beehive-shaped huts with cattle, consistent with the Frontier Wars in the Eastern Cape; the huts, dress, and setting are plausible Xhosa material culture, though the image is a European artist's depiction (Lucas, 1861) rather than an indigenous work.
